messages:
claire: Quick sync: following the RFC, proposing a pragmatic decomposition of the runtime into a thin request surface + capability plugins. Objective: reduce the monolith's cognitive load and make incremental paydown of routing/telemetry debt possible without a big-bang cutover. Thinking of an incremental "capability peel" where each capability (prefetching, prefix-cache, session-affinity, telemetry-enrich) is extracted behind a small HTTP/gRPC contract. Open to tradeoffs.

raj: I like incremental extraction. Two concerns: (1) interface churn risk if we over-index on current impl details, (2) tracing continuity across process boundaries. We need a versioned contract and trace ID propagation.

emily: For churn mitigation, recommend a strict contract lint and consumer-driven contract tests. We'll add a compatibility harness in CI that runs runtime + plugin shim. Also propose a 3-stage migration per capability: shim, read-only redirect, full control.

claire: Agreed. I'd add a 'compat shim' layer in the runtime that delegates to either in-process or remote plugin based on runtime flag so we can flip per node. That makes rollback cheap.

tom: Operational notes: extra network hop could affect tight p50 budgets. Suggest we co-locate plugins on same host (unix socket) for latency-sensitive hotpaths, and use loopback for spike. Also include a priority queue for hot-keys to avoid head-of-line blocking.

ops-bot: infra-task created: /infra/provision/local-socket-ns for early perf spikes (task 5273).

raj: On data ownership: we should aim to move ownership gradually. For prefix-cache, start with read-only plugin that sources from runtime cache then move writes once stable. For session-affinity, prefer plugin that owns session mapping to make routing simpler. Document edge cases for multi-instance failover.

emily: Testing checklist idea: unit contract tests, a dual-run integration (runtime+plugin shim), chaos test for plugin failure modes (timeouts/corruption), and a cost simulation job to estimate unit-cost delta with batching enabled. I'll draft CI jobs.

claire: Success criteria (proposal): 1) no more than +7ms p50 on the hotpath when plugin is remote; 2) p99 within +30ms; 3) rollout does not increase 95th percentile tail error budget; 4) observed unit-cost reduction or neutral after batching/caching optimizations. If we can't meet p99 we keep execution in-process for that tenant cohort.

tom: Rollout plan: stage 0 = spike with shim and loopback (1 week), stage 1 = small cohort read-only (2 weeks), stage 2 = write-path opt-in + canary by traffic (2 weeks), stage 3 = full flip and tech-debt tracker. Include a kill-switch for immediate revert.

raj: Security: plugins must inherit tenant identity tokens, validate signatures on contract calls, and respect KMS scoping. No plugin should have blanket tenant-wide KMS access; use short-lived credentials. I'll enumerate ACL mapping.

emily: Observability: require request-level tracing (trace_id header), token-level cost markers, and per-capability heatmaps. We should add a per-capability SLO dashboard and an alert when plugin-side latency contributes >50% of tail.

claire: Contract sketch for prefix cache (minimal):
```
POST /plugin/prefix_cache/lookup
headers: { x-tenant, x-trace-id }
body: { prefixes: ["pre_a","pre_b"], max_age_ms: 100 }
response: { entries: [{prefix: "pre_a", present: true, source: "mem|db", ts: 171234 }], warnings: [] }
```
Keep payload small and allow batched lookups.

raj: Also add an admin endpoint for pinning hot-keys for strong-consistency with explicit TTLs. That solves a few corner cases without forcing strong consistency everywhere.

emily: CI note: the compatibility harness should exercise the admin pin path and simulate node eviction to validate failover correctness.

claire: Action items: claire -> author follow-up RFC linking contract + stages; raj -> ACL/KMS mapping + threat primitives; emily -> CI harness + perf job; tom -> ops playbook + rollback steps. Aim to kick spike next Monday, no objections by COB Friday.

tom: +1. Will add the kill-switch and SRE oncall for stage 2.

raj: I'll scope the threat model and post by Wednesday.

emily: Will prototype shim today and post initial perf numbers tomorrow.

claire: Great. If anyone spots a coupling that would make extraction brittle please flag early. We'll keep the contracts intentionally tiny to avoid long-term coupling. Rolling unless objections.
